topic: THE 1966-1970 TALISMANS ARE THE MISSING PORTRAIT BOOKS FOR THIS BLOCK, AND THEY ARE NOT ON archive.org
note: archive.org holds 1943, 1946, 1947, 1963, 1964, 1965, then jumps to 1971-1981, 1986, 1987. There is NO 1966, 1967, 1968, 1969 or 1970 volume there, checked against the advancedsearch API. Twelve of this block's nineteen officers first served between 1966-67 and 1969-70, so their own class portraits are in exactly the five volumes archive.org does not have. That gap is why every earlier pass on this block fell back on the 1971 volume and on people outside the worklist. The five volumes DO exist on disk, pulled from TopSCHOLAR by an earlier run, at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/1966-1970/ as eight PDFs: tal1966, tal1967-pt1, tal1967-pt2, tal1968, tal1969-pt1, tal1969-pt2, tal1970-pt1, tal1970-pt2, 990 pages in all.

topic: THE EMBEDDED TEXT LAYER IN THE 1966-1970 TALISMANS IS WORTHLESS - AND THAT IS WHY NOBODY HAS WORKED THEM
note: All eight PDFs carry a text layer and it looks usable from a character count: 233,316 characters in the 1966 volume alone. It is unreadable rubbish. A real line comes out as 'Cill. ,;.,~", .. " P .... I,;,., " Am H,",",",,,,o. p",,;ri<n'_'. Searching it for a surname returns nothing: 'Spinnogatti' has zero hits in all eight volumes against the embedded layer. Any agent that greps these PDFs and concludes the people are not in them will be wrong. Re-OCR is not optional here, it is the only way in.

topic: NEW ASSET: THE 1966-1970 TALISMANS ARE NOW OCR'd, 990 PAGES
note: Built 5 September 2026 and kept at ~/Desktop/SGA60 photo hunt/_talisman-ocr-1966-1970/, one JSON per volume, about 2.8 MB. Every page of all eight PDFs, rendered at twice the scan's native pixel width and read with ocrmac (Apple Vision), stored as [{page, w, h, runs:[[text, confidence, [x,y,w,h] normalised]]}]. Quality is the difference between nothing and everything: the page that gives 'Cill. ,;.,~"' in the embedded layer gives 'Advisor: John Estill, Vice President; Karen Edmonds, President' from Vision. It runs at about one second a page, so the whole set rebuilds in twenty minutes on four workers. The bounding boxes are stored, so a name run can be turned straight into a crop rectangle. GREP THIS BEFORE RENDERING ANYTHING for 1966-1970.

topic: SCAN CEILING FOR 1966-1970: ONE SPREAD PER PAGE AT 1728 PIXELS
note: Every page of all eight PDFs is a single landscape image of a two-page spread, 1728 by 1152 pixels on a 1296 by 864 point page. That is 96 dpi, and it works out at about 864 by 1152 pixels for each printed page. It is the same ceiling recorded for the TopSCHOLAR Talismans of 1982-1991. A full-page studio portrait still cuts at around 480 by 630, which is good; a face in a class grid cuts at around 100 by 130, which is small but real; a face in a large group photograph is not worth cutting. Render with matrix zoom = native_image_width / page_width, then multiply by two for OCR only. Do not render at a fixed zoom.

topic: THE 1966-1970 VOLUMES CAPTION BY ROW, WHICH IS BETTER THAN THE 1970s ALPHABETICAL BLOCKS
note: From 1971 on, the Talisman class sections run alphabetical name blocks against a photograph grid and every identification is a counting argument. The 1966-1970 volumes do not. Their group photographs are captioned 'First Row: ... Second Row: ...' with the names enumerated in order, and their Who's Who and honours sections print a biographical block per person with that person's own portrait adjacent in the same column. Both are far more provable than a grid. Class section locations, by PDF page: tal1967-pt2 seniors 26-38, juniors 39-46, sophomores 47-57, freshmen 58-72. tal1968 seniors 126-139, juniors 140-150, sophomores 151-161, freshmen 162-178. tal1966 seniors 108-125. The 1969 and 1970 volumes hide their section headings from the embedded layer and have to be found through the new OCR index.

SETTLED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO. The College Heights Herald did NOT run a People Poll, or any photographed-students opinion feature, in the 1960s or 1970s. Do not send another agent after it. TWO INDEPENDENT PROOFS. (1) INDEX. In the WKU Archives' own item-level index of the whole digitised run (local mirror data/herald-index-full.json, 11,850 items) the string 'People Poll' occurs 295 times and every single one falls in 1993-1998, plus a later revival in 2011 and 2013. First occurrence 1993-01-26, 'People Poll: What Do You Think of Marriott After Its First Semester Here?'. Zero before 1993. The index is NOT thinner for the 1960s-70s, which is the objection that would otherwise kill this: restricted to actual College Heights Herald issues, 1966-1979 carries 728 issues at 29.3 index lines each, and 1993-1998 carries 336 issues at 30.4 lines each. Only 0.3 per cent of the 1966-79 lines hit the 300-character truncation cap, so CLAUDE.md's warning about truncated abstracts does not bite on this era. POSITIVE CONTROL: rank the recurring standing features and the 1993-98 list reads 'just a second' 84, 'campus line' 84, 'for the record' 84, 'people poll' 84 - the indexer records a standing feature every time it runs. The same ranking for 1966-1979 gives 'what's happening' 229, 'ombudsman' 48, 'alumni news' 40, 'coming events calendar' 40, 'editorial cartoon' 31, 'hilltopics' 25, and NOTHING resembling a photo poll anywhere in the top 35. (2) NEWSPRINT. Four Opinion pages pulled and looked at, spread across the range: 2 Nov 1967 (47:10, p.4), 1 Feb 1972 (51:32, p.4), 2 Mar 1976 (51:45, p.4) and 3 Oct 1978 (54:12, p.4, the page headed 'Opinion' outright). All four are the identical furniture: one or two set editorials, one editorial cartoon, the staff masthead, and 'Letters to the editor'. No photograph of a student appears on any of them. The 1976 page adds an 'Ombudsman' question-and-answer column and an 'Aberrations' column, both unillustrated. The feature simply does not exist in this era.

topic: THE OPINION-PAGE TRAP IS REAL AND IT NAMES OUR OWN OFFICERS - VERIFIED ON THE PAGE
note: The brief warned that letter-signature blocks mimic poll labels in OCR. Confirmed on the actual newsprint, and it is worse than a generic warning: it fires on THIS BLOCK'S OFFICERS LIST. The Herald sets a letter writer's name in bold, then class rank and dorm underneath on their own short lines - 'Randi Jensen / Publicity chairman, Associated Students / Junior / State Hall' on the Opinion page of 2 Nov 1967. Randi Jensen is officer number 6 on _officers-n6679.json. She is NOT PICTURED on that page; there is no photograph of any student on it. The block is a signature, nothing more. The 1972 page does the same for Nat Ritter, Hank L. Miles, Tim Brownlee, John Campbell, Fred Tutor and Jackie Aeberoold, and the 1978 page for Robert Riley and Barbara Hayes. Any agent that greps Herald OCR for an officer surname, finds it in a bold short-line block, and cuts the nearest photograph will produce a confident, sourced, WRONG portrait. On Herald Opinion pages, a name in bold is a byline or a signature until a caption proves otherwise.
